name: DCM Atlantic 1972: Red Storm Rising
description:
1 July 1972, 0000 Zulu. There has been no warning, and there will be no declaration. Within the hour the guns open along the whole length of the Iron Curtain; by first light the first echelon will be across the border, and our bombers over the airfields of Norway.

The plan is the Main Naval Staff's, and it is short. Tromsø first, then Copenhagen and Istanbul, then Trondheim, and last Reykjavík and Souda Bay. With the North Cape and the Straits in our hands the Baltic and Black Sea Fleets are free, and the Northern Fleet is out in the Atlantic before America can send a convoy across it.

The landing forces are loaded and at sea: the Northern Fleet's a few hours off Tromsø, the Baltic Fleet's east of Bornholm, the Black Sea Fleet's in the western Black Sea, closing the Bosporus. Our submarines lie across the lanes from Norfolk. NATO's ships are mostly in port, with Forrestal alongside at Norfolk; Saratoga and Independence are at sea, and they will answer within hours.

You command the Warsaw Pact at sea. Put the landings ashore, cut the Atlantic, and break the carriers when they come. The war ends when our flag flies over every base outside the United States and Canada, or when theirs flies over everything we hold beyond the Soviet Union and the Pact's own soil.

texts.guideWar: 1 July 1972, H-hour. The Warsaw Pact strikes first, without warning: North Norway and the Danish and Turkish Straits, then central Norway, Iceland and Crete, while the armies go for West Germany and Jutland. You command the Pact at sea: the Soviet Northern, Baltic and Black Sea Fleets (with the 5th Eskadra in the Mediterranean), and the East German, Polish, Bulgarian, Romanian, Egyptian and Syrian navies.
texts.guideWarTask: Three landing forces are already at sea and loaded: the Northern Fleet's for Tromsø, a few hours out; the Baltic Fleet's for Copenhagen, east of Bornholm; the Black Sea Fleet's for Istanbul, in the western Black Sea. Your first task is to put them ashore; then take Trondheim, Reykjavík and Souda Bay, and cut the Atlantic before the convoys from Norfolk can arrive.
texts.guideExampleMove: The Northern Fleet Strike Group holds north-west of Tromsø. Right-click the Norwegian Sea west of Bodø: it plots a sea route and shows its arrival time at each waypoint.
texts.guideExampleSplit: Split the Krivak Dostoynyy off the Northern Fleet Landing Group to escort a convoy into Tromsø once it is ours, then merge her back when the convoy is safely in.
texts.guideLift: Battalions ride in landing ships: Alligator 2 (the enemy's: Austin 2, Charleston or Newport 1, Fearless 2, Sir Lancelot 1).
texts.guideLiftIslands: Select the group and right-click an enemy port: every airfield here falls with its port.
texts.guideExampleInvade: The Northern Fleet Landing Group carries 6 battalions (three Alligators, 2 each). Tromsø, a minor port, is held by a garrison of 2; Norfolk, a naval base and depot, by 3. Bring gun escorts: their fire adds up to 50 %.
texts.guideDeckRates: the enemy's Forrestal 8, Enterprise 10; your Moskva and Leningrad are helicopter cruisers and launch nothing on the map
texts.guideExampleCarrier: Your Moskva and Leningrad carry only helicopters, and helicopters lost can't be replaced: keep them out of the enemy's air. Their magazines refill in port at a naval base, from its aviation stores. The enemy's Forrestal has her losses made good in port at a depot of his, such as Norfolk.
texts.guideReplen: The Kazbek (fuel) and the Boris Chilikin (fuel and some weapons) are in the Shipyard panel, under Replenishment (their card says what each carries). In a friendly port they load from its stock, never taking it below half of what it should hold.
texts.guideTanker: You have no tanker aircraft in this campaign: the game has no Soviet tanker of 1972, and the enemy has none on land either (his carriers' KA-3Bs aren't campaign tankers). How a tanker works:
texts.guideExampleStrike: The twelve MiG-27s of Black Sea Frontal Strike at Varna Airport with a Strike loadout on Çiğli before the Istanbul landing: fewer fighters to meet your landing ships.
texts.guideExampleSupply: Tromsø, once taken, is the next base to be fought for: set it to High so its missiles are topped up before the counter-attack comes.
texts.guideExampleIntel: "Signals intelligence reports a naval force of unknown size 140 nm from Keflavik": the red circle on the map is that area, not a firm position.
texts.guideCarrierPrices: Their price in the Shipyard panel. Carriers by tier: Moskva 300. Yours join with all their helicopters, at full price.
texts.guideVictory: The first side to hold every base in the theatre but those on the enemy's home soil wins: for you, all 69 NATO bases outside the United States and Canada, France, Italy, Greenland and Britain included; for the enemy, everything outside the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact countries, Alexandria, El Nouzha and Tartus included.
texts.guideRoad: Tromsø first (Langnes falls with it), then Copenhagen and Istanbul; then Trondheim, Reykjavík and Souda Bay, while the armies take West Germany and Jutland. Then the rest of Norway, the Faroes and Shetland; Den Helder, Brest, Lisbon and Gibraltar; Britain; the Mediterranean ports with Malta and Cyprus; last the Azores, Bermuda and Greenland.
texts.guideReplenStart: The Northern Fleet Tankers at Severomorsk, the Boris Chilikin with the Northern Fleet Strike Group and the Dmitry Galkin with the 5th Eskadra start loaded.
texts.guideBatteries: (Soviet: Redut coast-defence missiles and 2S3 guns; East Germany, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Egypt and Syria: BM-21 rockets; the enemy's NATO bases: M110 guns; Norway's: coastal guns)
texts.guideSams: (Soviet: SA-2, SA-3; East Germany, Egypt: SA-3; Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Syria: SA-2; the enemy's US, Iceland, Norway, Denmark, West Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Greece and Turkey: Nike Hercules; Britain: Rapier; Portugal, Canada and France: M42 guns, in place of SAM sites)
texts.guideEnemy: It starts on a peacetime footing, 181 ships, most in port. At sea are Saratoga's group in the Atlantic, Independence's in the central Mediterranean, an ASW group off Newfoundland, British escorts in the Western Approaches, and submarines from the Norwegian Sea to the Mediterranean. Its landings come one at a time: to take back Tromsø, Copenhagen, Reykjavík, Istanbul and Souda Bay, and for Tartus and Alexandria.
texts.guideSamReach: Nike Hercules 70 nm, SA-2 25, SA-3 15, Rapier 4
texts.endingWon: The last base the enemy held outside the United States and Canada has fallen. The American fleet is back behind its own coasts, NATO is gone from Europe, and the Atlantic is ours. The war is won.
texts.endingLost: The enemy holds every base we had beyond the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact countries. The convoys have got through, and what is left of the fleets has fallen back to the Kola, the Gulf of Finland and the Black Sea. The war is lost.
texts.procurementLift: a place in a landing ship (Alligator 2 · the enemy's Austin 2, Charleston or Newport 1)
texts.messageVictory: Victory. Every base outside the United States and Canada is ours: the campaign is won.
texts.messageDefeat: Defeat. The enemy holds every base we had beyond the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact countries: the campaign is lost.
texts.sitrepNote: The clock is paused: Space starts it
texts.sitrepNoteTip: Press Space, or Play in the time controls (top right), to start the clock. New to the campaign? The Guide (the book at the bottom of the left strip) starts with your first hour.

situation: As of 0000Z on 1 July the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact, with Egypt and Syria, are at war with NATO. No declaration has been made, and none will be.

The war plan of the Main Naval Staff is now in force. Its orders come in turn: Tromsø first, then Copenhagen and Istanbul, then Trondheim, and last Reykjavík and Souda Bay. West Germany and Jutland fall to the armies.

Three landing groups are loaded and at sea, each with its escorts in company: the Northern Fleet's north of Tromsø, the Baltic Fleet's east of Bornholm, the Black Sea Fleet's in the western Black Sea, closing the Bosporus.

Our submarines are on the lanes: Echo IIs in the Norwegian Sea, north of the Iceland-Faroes gap, Victors south of Iceland and off Halifax, Novembers and Foxtrots across the Atlantic, the 5th Eskadra's boats in the Ionian and the Sicilian Narrows.
Supply comes from Severodvinsk, Leningrad and Sevastopol. Every port we take must be fed by sea until it can feed the next landing.
enemy: By our last reports the enemy is on a peacetime footing, his ships mostly in port: the Royal Navy at Faslane and Portsmouth, the West Germans at Kiel and Wilhelmshaven, the Norwegians at Haakonsvern and Trondheim, the Italians, Greeks and Turks in their home bases. The American carrier Forrestal is reported alongside at Norfolk.

Two more American carriers are believed at sea: Saratoga somewhere in the Atlantic, Independence with the Sixth Fleet in the central Mediterranean. Neither position is firm. Finding them comes before anything else.
Expect him to wake quickly, and to answer within hours: first from the air, then with his carriers. P-3s from Keflavik, the Azores and Sigonella will be looking for our submarines.
Once roused, he will bring his carriers against our landings and run convoys from Norfolk under escort.
intent: Take Tromsø now, and with it North Norway: it opens the Norwegian Sea and covers the Kola.

Take the Danish Straits at Copenhagen and the Turkish Straits at Istanbul: they let the Baltic and Black Sea Fleets out. Then central Norway at Trondheim, and last Iceland at Reykjavík and Crete at Souda Bay. Every hour the enemy has to prepare is against us.
Strike the enemy's airfields before each landing goes in, and keep the escorts close round the landing ships.

Cut the Atlantic before America's convoys arrive. Submarines are to attack shipping on the lanes from Norfolk and Halifax and to report every movement. Without those convoys NATO cannot hold Britain or Europe.
Preserve the fleets, keep the sea lanes open, and be ready for the American counter-stroke.

starts.name: Barents Sea, off the Kola Inlet

firstOrder.title: Secure the Kola approaches
firstOrder.briefing: Every ship the Northern Fleet sends to the Norwegian Sea, and every tanker and transport behind it, must pass the mouth of the Kola Inlet. No American submarine is known in the Barents Sea tonight, but the first to get through will come here. Keep a ship of yours within 30 nm of Severomorsk for 12 hours in all within 2 days, and report any contact at once.

starts.name: Norwegian Sea, off the North Cape

firstOrder.title: Cover the Tromsø landing
firstOrder.briefing: The Northern Fleet Landing Group is a few hours from Tromsø with two Kresta Is, a Krivak and a Kashin in company, and Tromsø is the war plan's first order. Our last reports place the Norwegian fighters far to the south, at Ørland and Rygge, but the Kobben boats off Helgeland and the enemy's patrol aircraft will find the landing as soon as he wakes. Take station within 40 nm of the landing area north of Tromsø and keep a ship there for 24 hours in all within 2 days. Until Tromsø falls, your ships stand between the landing and the open sea.

starts.name: Norwegian Sea, north of the Faroes

firstOrder.title: Sink the radar pickets
firstOrder.briefing: Two old British destroyers are believed on radar picket between the Faroes and Shetland, to the south-east of you, watching the way into the Faroes-Shetland gap. While they report, every ship we send through is known at Keflavik and Faslane. Find them and sink at least one within 3 days. The F-4s and P-3s at Keflavik can reach you here, and American and British submarines are on this line: don't wait for them.

starts.name: Norwegian Sea, west of the Lofotens

firstOrder.title: Hunt the American boats
firstOrder.briefing: Two American attack submarines are believed on patrol to the south-west of you, in the middle of the Norwegian Sea, where they can reach the Northern Fleet's groups on their way to the Iceland-Faroes gap. They are quieter than anything we have. Go in slowly, listen first, and sink at least one of them within 4 days.

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Faslane
firstOrder.briefing: The Royal Navy's base on the Clyde, and everything the Americans mean to send to Britain, lives on the trunk lane from Norfolk, which passes some 65 nm to the south of you on its way to the North Channel. Get onto it and sink the tonnage this order asks for within 5 days, before the enemy can put escorts round his convoys. P-3s from Keflavik and the Azores will come looking: after each attack, shift your ground.

firstOrder.title: Hunt the Kobbens off Helgeland
firstOrder.briefing: Two Norwegian Kobben boats are believed on patrol off Helgeland, south of Vestfjorden, where they can reach the Northern Fleet Strike Group as it comes south and the ships that must follow the landing at Tromsø. Send out your patrol aircraft, find them and sink at least one within 4 days. Fighters cannot do this, and a reconnaissance Bear can only report what it finds: this is work for Il-38s. Small diesel boats on their own coast are hard to find.

firstOrder.title: Cover the Copenhagen landing
firstOrder.briefing: The Baltic Landing Group, with its cruiser and escorts, is in company with you east of Bornholm, and Copenhagen is the war plan's second objective. Its way lies across the Arkona Basin, between Bornholm and the Danish islands, where the West German destroyers at Kiel can reach it within hours. Take station within 40 nm of the marked point west of Bornholm and keep a ship there for 24 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Cover the Leningrad lane
firstOrder.briefing: Everything the Baltic Fleet burns and fires comes down the trunk lane from Leningrad to Kaliningrad, and NATO's submarines will come for it once the landings are under way. Ämari stands empty on the Estonian coast, a short flight from the lane, and it is yours to fill. Send Il-38s out on the mission Cover a lane (MISSION, Escort and cover) over it south-east of Gotland and keep it watched for 12 hours in all within 2 days; fighters cannot cover a lane. Report every contact to the Baltic Fleet.

firstOrder.title: Cover the Istanbul landing
firstOrder.briefing: The Black Sea Landing Group, with Moskva and Leningrad in company, is closing the mouth of the Bosporus from the open sea to the north-east, and Istanbul is the war plan's third objective. The Turkish destroyers are reported in port at Istanbul itself, a short run up the Bosporus from the landing, and the fighters at Çiğli can reach it too. Take station within 30 nm of the point off the mouth of the Bosporus and keep a ship there for 24 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Cover the Varna lane
firstOrder.briefing: The Black Sea Fleet's feeder lane from Sevastopol to Varna carries the stores for Varna and the Bulgarian fields, and it runs past you here. Until Istanbul falls, any boat that gets through the Straits will go for it first. Put your group on the mission Cover a lane (MISSION, Escort and cover) on the nearest stretch of it and keep it on station for 12 hours in all within 2 days. Report every contact to the Black Sea Fleet.

firstOrder.title: Strike the Independence group
firstOrder.briefing: The American carrier Independence is believed with the Sixth Fleet to the north-west of you, in the Ionian Sea, and she will turn on the 5th Eskadra within hours. Her strike aircraft reach further than your missiles: close her before she knows where you are. Find her group and sink at least one of its ships within 3 days. Expect the P-3s from Sigonella to find you first.

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Valletta
firstOrder.briefing: Malta lives on the lane from Naples: Valletta and RAF Luqa draw everything that way, down past Sicily to the east of you. With the 5th Eskadra's other boats spread through the Narrows, get onto that lane and sink the tonnage this order asks for within 5 days. The P-3s at Sigonella watch these waters: every attack gives the enemy a datum, so shift your ground after each one.
